text:
mira: Heads up — Marketing is planning a 48h fall promo next month. They estimate ~3x GAU during peak windows. Can infra run a quick runway sim for tokens/sec + concurrent requests? Need GPU-hour estimate, 95/99th latency headroom, and a ballpark cost delta for reserve vs preemptible.

sam: Yep. We can do a sim. Need model mix + avg sequence len distribution and whether we can assume prefix cache hit.

deepa: Model mix: 60% small-gen (redwood-small-v1), 30% medium-chat (redwood-chat-m), 10% long-form (redwood-long-qa). Avg seq len: p50=45 tokens, p90=220, p99=950. Prefix cache hit: assume 18% for chat flows, 5% for long-form.

sam: Good. I'll run a few sweeps: baseline traffic x3, x4 tail scenarios, and one with 20% longer sessions. Will capture tokens/sec, concurrent active requests, and KV cache pressure.

mira: Also include region split: 75% na, 20% eu, 5% apac. Marketing will target NA mostly.

ton y: @sam fyi we have limited spare dedicated in us-west this quarter — preemptible fallback will likely be needed for burst. How brittle is the tail if we route to preemptibles?

sam: Routing to preemptible reduces reserved throughput by ~30% for long requests due to spinup/warmup. For short gens it's ~10% latency hit if warm pools cold. Will quantify.

ana: small note on batching: if concurrency spikes, continuous batching can actually help throughput for small-gen but hurts 99th for long-form. We should simulate with two batching configs.

sam: plan: run 4 sims today — 
1) baseline x3 with current batching profile, prefix cache 18/5, region ratio
2) x3 but switch long-form to aggressive batching off
3) x4 tail + 20% longer session 
4) fallback plan: route overflow to preemptible region with 60s spinup penalty

sam: command I used:
```
run_tokensim --rps 12000 --model-mix "small:0.6,chat:0.3,long:0.1" --seq-pcts "50:45,90:220,99:950" --cache-hits "chat:0.18,long:0.05" --regions "na:0.75,eu:0.2,apac:0.05" --batch-config default
```
infra-bot: Job scheduled: tokensim-2026-11-03-07 (https://internal/runs/tokensim-2026-11-03-07). Estimated runtime ~18m.

jordan: For cost delta calc, do a reserve vs preemptible run with same throughput. Also include unit GPU-hour and egress roughing by region. If preemptible causes 15% more tokens due to retries, add that to cost.

sam: will add cost sweep. Quick ask: do we assume auto-scaling cooldown is 60s for dedicated? Current default is 90s for us-west. If we shorten to 60s we might reduce 99th but increase churn.

deepa: We can experiment. 60s cooldown means more warmup churn; simulate both 60 and 90.

mira: timeline? need a short brief for marketing by EOD tomorrow. Even rough numbers ok.

sam: I should have initial sims + a short deck by EOD tomorrow. Will post a short summary here with GPU-hour estimate and recommended fallback policy.

tony: If we decide to reserve extra for the window, we should prebook at least 72h before to guarantee placement in us-west. Keep that option on the table.

mira: Great. Thanks team. Please tag me when the summary is up. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: tokensim-2026-11-03-07 completed. Summary: baseline-x3 -> peak concurrent GPUs 38, tokens/sec 52k, estimated GPU-hours over 48h: 1824h. 99th lat above SLO for long-form under preemptible fallback in scenario 4. Detailed report: https://internal/runs/tokensim-2026-11-03-07/report.pdf

sam: Posting quick results: baseline x3 = 1824 GPU-hrs, cost w/ reserved pricing ~$92k, cost w/ 60% preemptible fallback ~$62k but 99th latency breaches for long-form by ~220ms. If we reserve 10 extra GPUs in us-west for promo window we drop preemptible need and keep 99th within SLO at cost ~$8k extra.

jordan: Thanks — can you add the retry/egress penalty numbers? I want to present cost with a conservative +12% retry overhead for preemptible scenarios.

sam: added note to report.

mira: This is gold. Will pass to marketing and ops. If we go reserve +10 GPUs, who owns the purchase? ops or finance?

ton y: ops handles provisioning but finance signs off for >$5k one-off. I'll loop in finance if we proceed.

mira: OK. Tagging @finance-next-step and will sync tomorrow. Thanks everyone.
